ideas.description: Exploit. Tests a proposed new H2.3 child: accuracy is set mainly in the final 32 px phase. This replaces I023, rebased on the current tip and with the direction stated unambiguously. On the E016 recipe (Muon with wd ×0.5, Lookahead/EMA, max-autotune with CUDA graphs, last group 512, LS 0.3), change only the resolution schedule. It goes from 24/28/32 px at 40/30/30% of steps to 24/32 px at 70/30%: every step that ran at 28 px now runs at 24 px, which means fewer pixels. The 32 px tail keeps its exact step count and position, and the LR and Lookahead/EMA schedules are unchanged. Build drops the 28 px graph and keeps warm-up and capture for 24 and 32 px with channels_last tensors from the training code path. error_on_recompile stays on after build.
ideas.expected: About 2.85 true epochs move from about 0.71 to 0.51 s/epoch (E012 timings), so time falls 7-9% (about 0.5-0.6 s), to about 6.0-6.1 s. Accuracy changes by -0.1 to -0.5 pp, to about 0.756-0.760, so the run stays feasible. A loss of 0.3 pp or less beats the epoch dial (about 1.9 s/pp) and supports tail-sets-accuracy; then cut 24 px epochs next. A loss above 0.5 pp means the middle phase matters, and resizing stops at 24/28/32.

ideas.description: Diagnostic, making no recipe change. It replaces I025, which pointed at E015, and answers the main crux of W1, W2, W3 and W5: is E016's 0.7607 real margin or a reshuffle? (1) Run the committed E016 recipe offline on held-out seeds 3-12 through the harness code path (benchmark.run --seed 3 --n 10). Record per-seed accuracy, the 10-seed mean, the std and the offset from 0.7607. (2) Secondary, for H4.3.1: clear the inductor cache and rebuild E016 in a fresh process, run seeds 0-2 again, and record whether the per-seed accuracies are bit-identical and how far the 3-seed mean shifts. (3) While doing this, read the true optimizer step count from the code for H4.2.3. E012's per-epoch timing listed 10 epoch loops, the last about half length, which suggests about 9.5 true epochs. Do not edit submissions/arena/.
ideas.expected: Time is unchanged at about 6.58 s. The held-out 10-seed mean is 0.757-0.760, an offset of -0.05 to -0.3 pp (E012 showed -0.08 pp for E010), and per-seed std is 0.15-0.35 pp. If the mean is at least 0.758, about 0.5 pp can be spent on A, C and D together. If it is at most 0.756, only one time cut fits before accuracy must be bought back. The rebuild is likely bit-identical; any non-identical seed means 3-seed keep decisions need 0.3 pp or more of headroom.

ideas.description: Exploit: spend the margin on the epoch dial. On the current tip, cut 1.0 true epoch uniformly. That is E016, about 9.5 → 8.5 true epochs (verify the step count in code first; H4.2.3). If the 24/32 swap idea was kept first, cut only 0.5 true epoch from it instead. Resolution phases stay fixed fractions of the total steps (so the 32 px tail keeps its 30% share), and the LR and Lookahead/EMA schedules stretch to the new step count, as in E008. Compiled shapes are unchanged, and error_on_recompile stays on.
ideas.expected: Time falls about 10% (about 0.65 s), to about 5.9 s on E016. Accuracy falls 0.3-0.7 pp, to about 0.754-0.758. Combined with E008 (-0.18 pp per 0.5 epoch), this gives a second slope point. A loss of 0.45 pp or less (about 1.45 s/pp or better) keeps the dial smooth. A loss above 0.7 pp means the curve steepens below about 9 epochs, so further time should come from FLOPs per sample, not epochs.

ideas.description: Explore/exploit on the biggest FLOP block. This replaces I028, rebased on E016. Group 2 (128→384 at 15×15, then two 384→384 convs at 7×7) is about 51% of conv MACs, and its width also feeds group 3's first conv. On the E016 recipe, narrow only group 2 from 384 to 320 channels (a multiple of 64, so tensor-core tiles stay aligned). Group 1 (128), group 3 (512), Muon lr and wd, epochs, the resizing schedule and Lookahead/EMA stay unchanged. Recapture every resolution's graph in build, with error_on_recompile on.
ideas.expected: Conv MACs fall about 16%, so time falls 7-10%, to about 5.95-6.1 s. Accuracy falls 0.2-0.6 pp, to about 0.755-0.758. The deciding number is the exchange rate. 2 s/pp or better (for example 0.55 s for 0.25 pp) beats the epoch dial and supports H2.5. Below 1.4 s/pp, which is E010's rate, means CIFAR-100 is width-sensitive and widths stay put.

ideas.description: Exploit, as a time-neutral accuracy booster that would fund the trims. E016's post-mortem points to the BN-bias wd (bias lr = 64 × lr) as the active part. On the E016 recipe, cut weight decay to ×0.25 of the original on the SGD groups only (BN biases, whitening bias, head), leaving the Muon conv-filter wd at E016's ×0.5. First check in code whether the filters are renormalized; if they are, filter wd is inert and this is equivalent to a global cut. Nothing else changes. Recapture the graphs if wd is baked in as a constant.
ideas.expected: Time is unchanged (±1%). Accuracy moves between -0.1 and +0.35 pp. A gain of at least 0.2 pp over E016 supports H1.5.3 and funds about 0.5 epoch more of trimming. A gain under 0.1 pp means the wd optimum is near ×0.5, so stop the wd grid. A loss of 0.2 pp or more means some bias decay is needed as regularization.

ideas.description: Explore a second FLOP lever with a different mechanism: depth at the highest-resolution stage. On the E016 recipe, remove only the third conv (128→128, with its BN-GELU) in group 1, keeping the residual and pooling structure otherwise intact. Group 1's maps are the largest, so its elementwise BN/GELU traffic is also the most memory-bound. Widths, optimizer, schedules, epochs and EMA stay unchanged. Recapture all resolutions in build, with error_on_recompile on.
ideas.expected: About 7% fewer conv MACs plus less memory-bound elementwise work, so time falls 5-9%, to about 6.0-6.25 s. Accuracy falls 0.15-0.6 pp. A rate of 1.9 s/pp or better supports H2.5.2 and makes this a cheaper cut than group-2 width. A loss above 0.5 pp means early depth matters for 100 classes.

ideas.description: Explore. This is the single-factor version of E011, separating its two confounded changes. On the E016 recipe, change only the first phase: the first 15% of steps run at 20 px, followed by 24 px for 25%, 28 px for 30% and 32 px for 30%. The 32 px tail keeps its exact step count and position, and the LR and EMA schedules are unchanged. Warm up and capture the 20 px graph in build with channels_last tensors from the training code path, with error_on_recompile on.
ideas.expected: Pixel-weighted cost falls about 3.5%. E011 ran slightly faster than proportional, so time falls 3.5-5%, to about 6.25-6.35 s. Accuracy changes by -0.05 to -0.35 pp. A loss of 0.2 pp or less with time down at least 4% supports H2.3.2 and pins E011's cliff on the shortened 32 px tail, not on the 20 px phase. A loss above 0.35 pp means 20 px itself is harmful on 100 classes.

drop.reason: Time-neutral mechanism test with no route to a better score: the committee agrees (conflict 0, 1/5 improve votes) that plain EMA will land at or below the Lookahead tip. Even if it matched, nothing gets faster.
Rewritten as the 24/32 px swap idea on the E016 tip. The 0.5 conflict came from a member misreading the direction (28→32 instead of 28→24), so the new text states that 28 px steps become 24 px steps.

Superseded. The tail-sets-accuracy crux is tested more cleanly and with a larger time saving by the 24/32 swap, and the epoch dial by the uniform 1.0-epoch trim (H4.2.4) on E016. The 24 px-only cut can come back after the swap result.
Pointed at E015, which is no longer the tip. Rewritten as the E016 held-out-seed and rebuild diagnostic (H4.1.3 plus H4.3.1).
All committee members forecast no effect (0/4 improve votes), and the Muon scalar knobs (lr, LS) have been flat within noise. Low information, low expected gain.
Rewritten as the group-2 narrowing idea on the E016 tip, which now carries the halved wd. The old version targeted E015.

structured_output.summary:
The tip is E016: 0.7607 accuracy, 6.58 s. That leaves about 0.77 pp of local margin to spend on time. The queue moves from finding accuracy boosters to spending that margin on time cuts, in order of expected time saved per pp lost. Every rebased idea now builds on E016, not E015.

1. **24/32 px swap (priority 5).** The 28 px phase becomes 24 px and the 32 px tail is left untouched. This is the largest cheap cut (about -8%) and tests the committee's shared "tail sets accuracy" crux.
2. **E016 held-out diagnostic (priority 4).** Runs held-out seeds 3-12 plus a fresh-cache rebuild. Every member's top crux is how much of E016's margin is real.
3. **Uniform trim of 1.0 true epoch (priority 4).** This gives a second slope point for the epoch dial. E012's per-epoch timing shows 10 epoch loops with a half-length last one, which suggests about 9.5 true epochs (H4.2.3). The step count should be checked in code first.
4. **Group 2 narrowed to 320 channels (priority 3).** Group 2 holds about half the conv MACs.
5. **Lower wd on the SGD groups only (priority 3).** A time-neutral booster that targets the BN-bias decay mechanism from the E016 post-mortem.
6. **Exploration (priority 2):** drop group 1's third conv, and add a 20 px phase over the first 15% of steps with the 30% tail kept. The second test separates E011's two confounded changes.

Dropped:
- **I022:** a mechanism test with no time payoff.
- **I027:** Muon momentum; the committee forecasts it flat.
- **I023, I025, I028:** rewritten on E016. I023 also had its direction stated unambiguously, since its 0.5 conflict came from a member reading it backwards.
- **I024:** superseded by the swap plus the uniform trim.

BN recalibration and the bs-1250 test stay off the queue under the committee's veto. I021 (the graph-break and profile check) is still running.
